292: /* Search a skip list */
293: 
294: int caml_lf_skiplist_find(struct lf_skiplist *sk, uintnat key, uintnat *data) {
295:   const struct lf_skipcell *found_cell = lf_skiplist_lookup(sk, key, NULL);
296: 
297:   if (found_cell->key == key) {
298:     if (data) {
299:       *data = found_cell->data;
300:     }
301:     return 1;
302:   } else {
303:     return 0;
304:   }
305: }
306: 
307: int caml_lf_skiplist_find_below(struct lf_skiplist *sk, uintnat k, uintnat *key,
308:                                 uintnat *data) {
309:   struct lf_skipcell *pred;
310:   struct lf_skipcell *curr = lf_skiplist_lookup(sk, k, &pred);
311:   const struct lf_skipcell *found_cell;
312: 
313:   if (curr->key == k) {
314:     found_cell = curr;
315:   } else if (pred != sk->head) {
316:     found_cell = pred;
317:   } else {
318:     return 0;
319:   }
320: 
321:   if (data) {
322:     *data = found_cell->data;
323:   }
324:   if (key) {
325:     *key = found_cell->key;
326:   }
327:   return 1;
328: }
329: 
330: /* Insertion in a skip list */
331: 
332: int caml_lf_skiplist_insert(struct lf_skiplist *sk, uintnat key, uintnat data) {
333:   struct lf_skipcell *preds[NUM_LEVELS];
334:   struct lf_skipcell *succs[NUM_LEVELS];
335: 
336:   CAMLassert(0 < key);
337:   CAMLassert(key < CAML_UINTNAT_MAX);
338: 
339:   while (1) {
340:     /* We first try to find a node with [key] in the skip list. If it exists
341:        then we don't need to add it. The [skiplist_find] method will also
342:        populate the predecessors and successors arrays, which gives us the nodes
343:        between which we could add the new node. */
344:     int found = skiplist_find(sk, key, preds, succs);
345:     struct lf_skipcell *pred;
346:     struct lf_skipcell *succ;
347: 
348:     if (found) {
349:       /* Already present; update data */
350:       atomic_store_relaxed((atomic_uintnat*)&succs[0]->data, data);
351:       return 1;
352:     } else {
353:       /* node does not exist. We need to generate a random top_level and
354:        * construct a new node. The new node's forward array (which contains the
355:        * next node in increasing order of key, at each level) starts at
356:        * [top_level] and goes to 0. Each entry will point to the successors in
357:          the [succ] array for that level. */
358:       int top_level = random_level();
359:       /* sufficiently aligned for LF_SK_MARK/UNMARK */
360:       struct lf_skipcell *new_cell = caml_stat_alloc_noexc(
361:           SIZEOF_LF_SKIPCELL + (top_level + 1) * sizeof(struct lf_skipcell *));
362:       if (new_cell == NULL)
363:         caml_fatal_error("caml_lf_skiplist_insert: out of memory");
364:       new_cell->top_level = top_level;
365:       new_cell->key = key;
366:       new_cell->data = data;
367:       atomic_store_relaxed(&new_cell->garbage_next,NULL);
368: 
369:       for (int level = 0; level <= top_level; level++) {
370:         atomic_store_release(&new_cell->forward[level], succs[level]);
371:       }
372: 
373:       /* Now we need to actually slip the node in. We start at the bottom-most
374:          level (i.e the linked list of all nodes). This is because all searches
375:          must end up at this level and so as long as the node is present, it
376:          will be found - regardless of whether it has been added to the level
377:          above. Consider the staircasing referred to in [skiplist_find] earlier,
378:          the final step in finding a node is following the reference from its
379:          predecessor at the bottom level. */
380:       pred = preds[0];
381:       succ = succs[0];
382: 
383:       /* We could be racing another insertion here and if we are then restart
384:          the whole insertion process. We can't just retry the CAS because the
385:          new node's predecessor and successors could have changed. There's also
386:          a possibility that the predecessor's forward pointer could have been
387:          marked and we would fail the CAS for that reason too. In that case the
388:          [skiplist_find] earlier on will take care of snipping the node before
389:          we get back to this point. */
390:       if (!atomic_compare_exchange_strong(&pred->forward[0], &succ, new_cell)) {
391:         caml_stat_free(new_cell);
392:         continue;
393:       }
394: 
395:       for (int level = 1; level <= top_level; level++) {
396:         while (1) {
397:           pred = preds[level];
398:           succ = succs[level];
399: 
400:           /* If we were able to insert the node then we proceed to the next
401:              level */
402:           if (atomic_compare_exchange_strong(&pred->forward[level], &succ,
403:                                              new_cell)) {
404:             break;
405:           }
406: 
407:           /* On the other hand if we failed it might be because the pointer was
408:              marked or because a new node was added between pred and succ nodes
409:              at level. In both cases we can fix things by calling
410:              [skiplist_find] and repopulating preds and succs */
411:           skiplist_find(sk, key, preds, succs);
412:         }
413:       }
414: 
415:       /* If we put the new node at a higher level than the current
416:          [search_level] then to speed up searches we need to bump it. We don't
417:          care too much if this fails though. */
418:       if (top_level > atomic_load_relaxed(&sk->search_level)) {
419:         atomic_store_relaxed(&sk->search_level, top_level);
420:       }
421: 
422:       return 1;
423:     }
424:   }
425: }
426: 
427: /* Deletion in a skip list */
428: 
429: int caml_lf_skiplist_remove(struct lf_skiplist *sk, uintnat key) {
430:   struct lf_skipcell *preds[NUM_LEVELS];
431:   struct lf_skipcell *succs[NUM_LEVELS];
432:   struct lf_skipcell *succ;
433:   int marked;
434: 
435:   /* As with insert. If the node doesn't exist, we don't need to do anything.
436:      While we're checking for it we populate the predecessor nodes and successor
437:      nodes at each level. */
438:   int found = skiplist_find(sk, key, preds, succs);
439: 
440:   if (!found) {
441:     return 0;
442:   } else {
443:     /* When the node exists in the skiplist, then succs[0] must point to it.
444:        Note: this isn't the case for levels > 0. */
445:     struct lf_skipcell *to_remove = succs[0];
446:     for (int level = to_remove->top_level; level >= 1; level--) {
447:       /* We mark each of the forward pointers at every level the node is present
448:          at. We may be raced by another thread deleting the same node and by
449:          threads inserting new nodes directly after the node we are removing,
450:          so we need to retry the CAS in a loop to deal with the latter. */
451:       LF_SK_EXTRACT(to_remove->forward[level], marked, succ);
452: 
453:       while (!marked) {
454:         atomic_compare_exchange_strong(&to_remove->forward[level], &succ,
455:                                        LF_SK_MARKED(succ));
456:         LF_SK_EXTRACT(to_remove->forward[level], marked, succ);
457:       }
458:     }
459: 
460:     /* The bottom layer is what ultimately determines whether the node is
461:        present in the skiplist or not. We try to remove it and if we succeed
462:        then indicate so to the caller. If not then another thread raced us an
463:        won. */
464:     LF_SK_EXTRACT(to_remove->forward[0], marked, succ);
465:     while (1) {
466:       int mark_success = atomic_compare_exchange_strong(
467:           &to_remove->forward[0], &succ, LF_SK_MARKED(succ));
468: 
469:       LF_SK_EXTRACT(to_remove->forward[0], marked, succ);
470: 
471:       if (mark_success) {
472:         skiplist_find(sk, key, preds, succs); /* This will fix up the mark */
473:         return 1;
474:       } else if (marked) {
475:         return 0; /* Someone else beat us to removing it */
476:       }
477: 
478:       /* If we end up here then we lost to a thread inserting a node directly
479:          after the node we were removing. That's why we move on one successor.
480:        */
481:     }
482:   }
483: }
484: 
485: /* Collects freed nodes from the skiplist. This must be called periodically from
486:    a single thread at a time when there can be no concurrent access to this
487:    skiplist */
488: 
489: void caml_lf_skiplist_free_garbage(struct lf_skiplist *sk) {
490:   struct lf_skipcell *curr = atomic_load_acquire(&sk->garbage_head);
491: 
492:   const struct lf_skipcell *head = sk->head;
493:   while (curr != head) {

The compiler now builds cleanly and all 40 tests in the basic testsuite pass.

**Bug summary:** In `runtime/shared_heap.c`'s `pool_sweep`, the run-length compression of free blocks conflicted with how the loop advanced across blocks. The loop was using `p += Whsize_hd(hd)` for both live and free blocks, but for a free block whose header's `Wosize_hd` represents *additional free blocks after the current one*, `Whsize_hd` gives the wrong number of words (it gives `Wosize_hd + 1` words but the block physically occupies `wh` words). Likewise, for live blocks `Whsize_hd(hd)` may be less than `wh`, leaving the pointer inside the padding of the slot rather than at the next `wh`-aligned block. Both cases were fixed by advancing `p += wh` per block (after `p += wh * Wosize_hd(hd)` to skip the extra free blocks in a run), matching the pattern used everywhere else in the file (`pool_finalise`, `calc_pool_stats`, `verify_pool`, `compact_update_pools`, etc.).
